newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian power firm head hopes to dispel bad luck.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian power firm head hopes to dispel bad luck.

text.p: In a bid to appease the gods, the head of Malaysia's national utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd has changed the name of an inauspiciously termed power outage index, a newspaper reported.

The Star reported on Saturday that Ahmad Tajuddin Ali, who took over as Tenaga executive chairman in September after the utility's second major blackout in four years, was not keen on the term used to measure the occurrence of power outages.
The industry uses the term "supply unavailability index" or SUI, in short, as the yardstick. "When pronounced 'su-ay', the word means 'bad luck' in a Chinese dialect," the newspaper said.

Although not superstitious, Tajuddin has said he does not find the name funny in light of Tenaga's woes, and the nuclear engineer has changed the name to "supply availability index", the article said.
Peninsula Malaysia suffered a blackout of up to 15 hours on August 3, which led to a management shake-up at the state-controlled utility and fresh scrutiny of its operations.
